findings.title: Identity is custom school accounts, not Supabase Auth
findings.finding: public.accounts.id and organization_id are UUIDs. Opaque bearer tokens are SHA-256 hashed and checked by service-role api_session_lookup against private.sessions. All 11 configured Edge Functions disable gateway JWT verification intentionally; ordinary account APIs must perform their own lookup/role checks. setup-api and login-diagnostics instead use a bootstrap secret.
findings.action: Extend existing account identities/capabilities. Do not use auth.uid() = accounts.id or introduce a parallel authentication system.

findings.title: RLS is deny-direct with Edge service-role authorization
findings.finding: Foundational and newer protected tables enable RLS; explicit anon/authenticated revokes cover foundations, mastery, private banks/uploads and readiness. No CREATE POLICY or auth.uid() use was found in canonical migrations. Lesson visibility and timetable migrations enable RLS but do not independently restate table grants/revokes. Effective deployed grants were not queried.
findings.action: New foundation tables must explicitly enable RLS and revoke PUBLIC/anon/authenticated access and RPC execution. Grant only service_role. Add executable isolated database role tests; source-marker checks alone are insufficient.

findings.title: Current identifiers collapse curriculum versions and AB/BC
findings.finding: Class course_key/academic_year are text. canonicalCourseKey collapses AP AB and BC into ap-calculus. lesson_catalog keys are (organization_id,access_key), completions (account_id,access_key), mastery (account_id,skill_key), and trust (question_id). None identifies curriculum or lesson content version. readiness_models has its own integer model version and diagnostic_version is text; neither is a curriculum version.
findings.action: Add immutable curriculum/course/lesson versions and explicit class/cohort assignment tables alongside legacy keys. Preserve alias adapters for existing URLs but never infer new AB/BC or IB syllabus identity from an old alias. Do not overwrite or backfill existing evidence without an explicit audited mapping.

findings.title: Class membership writes do not enforce tenant and account-role consistency
findings.finding: class_memberships has only class_id/account_id UUID FKs and membership_role check; these do not ensure both records share an organization or that membership_role matches account role. setMembers checks access to the target class, then deletes all memberships and inserts caller-supplied UUIDs without candidate-account org/status/role validation or a transaction. Failure after delete can leave membership loss.
findings.action: Do not reuse this mutation for new cohort assignments. Use tenant-consistent FK design and transactional validated operations with cross-org, role-mismatch and failed-write rollback tests. Treat baseline remediation as a separate approved narrow slice.

findings.title: Lesson release and progression are completion based
findings.finding: Catalog rows are organization-wide mutable current routes. Students need an active matching class. Explicit hidden/shown overrides are evaluated per class; any class allowing wins. First two ready positions are automatic; later positions need previous lesson completion plus nonempty completed practice session. These completion/session values originate in authenticated client uploads, not verified mastery.
findings.action: Keep current release semantics behind an adapter. New version/cohort publication must not silently reinterpret legacy completion as mastery, share completions across versions, or let one cohort override another unintentionally.

findings.title: Active mastery bridge bypasses account-owned queues and drops evidence
findings.finding: institution-experience dynamically loads institution-mastery-evidence on dashboards. The bridge replaces canonical syncLearning/flushPending, stores one global unowned pending payload, and flushes it under current credentials. Its exportStudentReport-based builder expects raw arrays absent from the actual summary report, and never includes lessons. The canonical client already collects raw engine arrays and lesson completions and uses account-owned pending envelopes. Isolated VM execution of all three unmodified source files reproduces cross-account replay and raw evidence/completion loss; canonical queue control passes. Event callbacks retain closed-over canonical functions, so these exported overrides coexist with the compatibility path. This is not a production-state claim.
findings.action: Reproduce with local VM/browser harness. Then centralize payload and owned queue logic, preserving mastery-evidence recomputation; make bridge delegate, support completions on the authoritative sync route, and test account changes/offline replay/summary-vs-raw engine shape.

findings.title: Server-computed mastery is not fully server-validated evidence
findings.finding: The database rejects client mastery records and overwrites attempt trust tier. However mastery-evidence accepts client correctness, skill, assistance, difficulty, representation and timestamps; all trust tiers participate in scoring. Verified question evidence adds a confidence bonus but is not required by last_verified_at thresholds. No answer-key validation or enrolled-course/assignment check is present in ingestion. APCALC-prefixed skill input bypasses atomic remapping.
findings.action: Preserve current guardrails and distinguish aggregation authority from evidence authenticity. New versioned records should carry server-resolved question/content version/skill and evidence provenance. Stronger grading/evidence authorization requires its own design and executable tests.

findings.title: Atomic DB remapping and recomputation use different skill identities
findings.finding: The atomic attempt trigger may replace an ambiguous legacy skill key with its unique APCALC skill. recomputeMastery is invoked using pre-insert attemptRows skill keys, then queries database rows only for those keys. An inserted row remapped by the trigger may not be included in that immediate recomputation. The query also takes the first 10,000 ascending attempts, which can omit later evidence once an account exceeds that total for affected skills.
findings.action: Test unique atomic remap with stored return rows and high-volume evidence before relying on this path for new curriculum versions; resolve canonical stored skills and define bounded aggregation semantics.

findings.title: Older backend access routes remain reachable beside newer guards
findings.finding: practice-bank-api requires assigned course and student lesson/unit scope but does not itself call lesson progression checks; assignedCourses omits active-class and organization filters used by institution lesson access. private-bank-api older student question/detail/media handlers check organization/readiness but not enrollment/dedicated-course scope. institution-api /learning/sync still attempts client mastery writes; the authority trigger should reject those while parallel non-mastery writes can succeed first.
findings.action: Do not integrate new curricula through legacy bypass routes. Add negative endpoint integration tests for unassigned/archived/cross-org classes, hidden lessons, foreign assignments and older API aliases; consolidate authoritative policy separately.

findings.title: Private bank release already has rights and trust contracts
findings.finding: The latest release trigger allows at least one verified lesson/skill mapping and enforces publisher-key or independent-solution-audit evidence plus rights.student_publication_allowed. Mapping index triggers and practice inventory RPC support imported bank routes. Media is private and signed temporarily. New lesson publication must not bypass these gates or publish private payloads to Pages.
findings.action: Attach versioned mapping/provenance to existing bank contracts rather than duplicating question stores or weakening ready/rights checks.

findings.title: Merging backend migrations to main auto-applies production changes
findings.finding: deploy-institution-backend triggers on main changes to migrations/functions, runs source validators, links production, performs db push, and deploys all Edge Functions. Existing checks cover source contracts and selected pure JS logic, not full isolated PostgreSQL tenant/RLS/FK lifecycle tests.
findings.action: ECHS003 must include executable isolated database tests before merge. Initially create only additive, deny-direct schema with no runtime integration. Verify fresh migration chain, rollback-by-forward-migration, tenant constraints and role grants. Do not run production diagnostics as part of this audit.
